nodes.answer: The paragraph introduces a relational approach as the analytical lens.

Climate shocks, data-driven sustainability, and producer engagement with digital technology This section examines work published on climate shocks and the risks they pose, the shift toward data-driven sustain - ability solutions, and the ways in which an emphasis on pro - ducers engagement with digital technologies contributes to scholarly understanding of how producers prepare for and respond to shocks. 1 354 Digital technology and on-farm responses to climate shocks: exploring the relations between producer agency Climate shocks Shocks, as sudden and unpredictable events, are of interest in the scholarship of food and agriculture due to their far- reaching effects. nodes.answer: Digital technologies can gather complete and accurate data, helping decision-makers identify effective solutions for reducing environmental impact.

Specifically, DTs optimise the data acquisition, collection, and management pro- cesses, ensuring greater transparency and traceability (Zhang et al. 2020; Carri res et al. 2021; Mogos and Fragapane 2022; Sica et al. 2022). By implementing advanced systems, they also increase the sharing processes and security of data trans- mission (Huang et al. 2020 ; Sica et al. 2022 ; Dervishaj and Gudmundsson 2024). For instance, the inventory phase can benefit from digital technologies by gathering complete and accurate data, supporting decision-makers in identifying effec- tive solutions for reducing environmental impact (Zhang et al. 2020). nodes.question: What are the main barriers to integrating digital technologies into LCA?
nodes.answer: The main barriers include the need for advanced technical skills, high initial costs, resistance to change within organizations, lack of standardization and interoperability between digital tools, and data protection and privacy concerns.

This approach boosts innovation in production processes and improves corporate sustainability, fostering the twin digi - tal and circular transition (Nascimento et al. 2019; Bai et al. 2020 ; Bocken et al. 2023). Despite the benefits, integrating digital technologies into LCA is a complex process as it is still at an early stage of study and implementation (Wang et al. 2019; Sica et al. 2022). The main barriers to improvements in these terms include the need for advanced technical skills to implement and manage these technologies, high initial costs associated with the adoption of new digital infrastructure, and resistance to change within organisations (Farooque et al. 2020; Ruggieri et al. 2020). In addition, the lack of standardi- sation and interoperability between different digital tools and platforms can complicate data integration and hinder the effec- tiveness of assessments (Ghita et al. 2021 ). nodes.answer: It indicates an increase in the availability and adoption of feedback-based digital solutions like in-home energy displays, web portals, and smartphone-based energy apps.

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What opportunity arose from the increase in reliance on digital tools during the COVID-19 pandemic?
nodes.answer: The shift during the pandemic created opportunities for digital energy solutions, such as smart energy apps, to play a greater role in household energy management.
nodes.paragraph: Further, Wemyss et al. (2023) emphasise the importance of moving beyond the initial excite- ment around these technologies to understand better the conditions under which they function as social innovations contributing to low-carbon transitions. This perspective underscores the need to study energy apps as mediators of user engage- ment, providing insight into how digital interfaces influence interactions with energy data and inform decision-making. The COVID-19 pandemic has further amplified interest in digital solutions that support sustain- able lifestyles as environmental awareness became a more salient priority for consumers (World Eco- nomic Forum, 2020). Lockdowns and remote work increased reliance on digital tools for managing daily activities, including energy consumption (Gunaratna & Aslam, 2022). This shift created opportunities for digital energy solutions, such as smart energy apps, to play a greater role in household energy manage- ment. Verplanken and Wood (2006) highlight that smart energy technologies, including energy apps, can encourage reflective energy use by providing actionable feedback. Similarly, Sanguinetti et al. (2018) emphasise that user interaction with these technologies can enhance awareness of energy-effi- cient practices.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the focus of the recent study mentioned in the paragraph regarding digital energy platforms?
nodes.answer: The recent study focuses on how users engage with digital energy platforms by analyzing app reviews to explore perceptions, evaluations, and points of interaction.
nodes.paragraph: However, Huijer, (2013) observes the effectiveness of these tools and examines how well they integrate with users existing practices and routines. Furthermore, Chalal et al., (2022) conducted a systematic review of energy eco-feedback systems, highlighting the importance of effective visualisation techniques in enhancing user engagement and com- prehension of energy consumption patterns. Recent work by Mosca et al., (2024) maps the landscape of digital interventions to promote sustainability, calling for future studies on effective digital interventions. This study builds on this literature by focusing on how users engage with digital energy platforms, using app reviews as a lens to explore perceptions, evalua- tions, and points of interaction. Relevance of user reviews Analysing user reviews for smart energy apps can offer valuable insights into users perceptions and interactions with these technologies. Particularly, such reviews can highlight how users engage with app features, their awareness of energy feedback, and their perceptions of the app S utility in supporting informed energy decisions. This approach aligns with the growing recognition of energy big data S potential to enhance efficiency by analysing user dimensions (Zhou & Yang, 2016).
